newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods static amid volatile NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods static amid volatile NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. West Coast bulk product prices were static early Wednesday as buyers and sellers weathered a volatile NYMEX session and saw supplies rise on weak motorist demand out West, brokers said.

Spot trade dried up as NYMEX crude and products gave western dealers little direction. February heating oil jumped two cents a gallon after an early downturn, while crude settled 84 cents a barrel above Tuesday's market.
Supplies of gasoline in PADD 5 built by 623,000 barrels last week despite local refiners operating at 84.6 percent of capacity, a 4.9 percentage point decrease during the week.
Gasoline supplies stood at 29.5 million barrels in the West Coast.
Traders also said inventories built at supply terminals because poor weather in recent weeks has lowered motorist demand.

A Salomon Brothers report released Wednesday showed the dealer tank wagon market, a gauge of prices charged at terminals, fell below spot prices during the fourth quarter as intense battles for market share in southern California forced cuts in retail prices.
CARB gasoline prices for January delivery were flat at 76/77.50 cents a gallon in Los Angeles. Conventional gasoline was unchanged 74/75 cents a gallon.
Meanwhile, low sulphur diesel fuel in L.A. did see an advance amid sharply higher heating oil futures.
